record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.original_question: Consider the maximal immediate extensions of the valued fields Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) produced in Kartas's work, where some of these maximal immediate extensions have decidable elementary theories and uncountably many have distinct elementary theories. What is the structure of these maximal immediate extensions, beyond the fact that they are infinite, and which structural features distinguish the decidable extensions from the undecidable ones?

evidence.quote:
Kartas shows that there are uncountably many maximal immediate extensions
with distinct elementary Lval-theories. This implies that uncountably many of them
are not decidable.

Open problem 2: What is the structure of these extensions (apart from the fact
that they are infinite)? What are the indications in their structure that distinguish
the decidable from the undecidable extensions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let p be a prime number. Consider the valued fields K_1 = Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}), the cyclotomic extension of Q_p obtained by adjoining all p-power roots of unity, and K_2 = Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}), the field obtained by adjoining all p-power roots of p, both equipped with the unique extension of the p-adic valuation. A valued field extension L/K is called immediate if it induces no extension on the value group and no extension on the residue field. A maximal immediate extension of (K, v) is one that admits no proper immediate extension.

It is known that each of K_1 and K_2 admits uncountably many maximal immediate extensions whose elementary theories in the language L_val of valued fields are pairwise distinct, and consequently uncountably many of these maximal immediate extensions have undecidable L_val-theory, while certain (specifically constructed) maximal immediate extensions are known to have decidable L_val-theory.

Problem: Beyond the fact that they are of infinite transcendence degree over K_i, describe the algebraic, valuation-theoretic, and model-theoretic structure of the maximal immediate extensions of K_1 and of K_2. In particular, identify intrinsic structural invariants or features (for instance, properties of pseudo-Cauchy sequences, Kaplansky-type defect data, generating sets, or definable subsets) that distinguish those maximal immediate extensions whose L_val-theory is decidable from those whose L_val-theory is undecidable.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent (2025) survey on model theory of tame valued fields. Kartas's work establishes the existence of uncountably many maximal immediate extensions of Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) with pairwise distinct elementary theories (so most are undecidable), while exhibiting some with decidable theory; no published structural classification distinguishing decidable from undecidable cases was found.

status_evidence.title: Decidability via the tilting correspondence — K. Kartas
status_evidence.snippet: Kartas proves relative decidability results for perfectoid-type fields including Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}), and constructs maximal immediate extensions with distinct elementary theories.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the decidability/undecidability landscape of maximal immediate extensions referenced in the open problem, but does not give a structural classification.
